reasoning: I compared the genuine claim with the planted one. It differs only in sec. 4's first_end date, which is now 2001-12-28. I re-hashed every cited text and re-checked every quoted span (all match). Identity is confirmed: EO 13251 of Dec. 28, 2001, 67 FR 1599, State Department succession under the Federal Vacancies Reform Act. The 34 clauses cover the full text, with the documented merges of headings and items too short to verify. Sec. 4's revocation of EO 12343 was performed on issuance on 2001-12-28; the order has no separate effective-date clause, so the actor (EO 13251) and the mechanism are correct and now consistent with the reasons. EO 13261 sec. 4(i), signed 2002-03-19 with no effective-date clause, replaced sec. 3(b), and the before and after texts match the held bytes. The OFR notes (Revokes EO 12343; Amended by EO 13261) are addressed. The number search finds no revocation or supersession, and the 2010 notice citing '13251' is correctly identified as a mistaken authority line. No clause has an own-terms end, and the operative clauses rest on the original text plus the bounded searches through 2026-10-14. Savings: none needed.
